description: Store a memory (markdown body). Describe it on three axes: `project` (which body of work - e.g. kythene, haven), `type` (the KIND of note - decision, how-to, gotcha, reference, person, meeting), and `tags` (what it is ABOUT - auth, billing, postgres). A kind-word like `decision` is a `type`, not a tag; `type` is optional but set it when the note has a kind. Keep knowledge current by superseding rather than duplicating: set `supersedes` to the exact id of the memory to replace (it replaces that memory whatever its title, so it can also fix a near-miss title fork), or on the conversational path re-use a title within a project. Optional `aliases` add extra names a [[wikilink]] can use to reach this memory. Set `private` when only you should see it; the response `restricted` flag reports whether it was stored private (from `private`, or auto-scoped because it drew on restricted content you read). Follow the workspace guide for house style, taxonomy and what belongs - see get_workspace_guide, also returned inline by recall as `guide`.

aliases.description:
aliases are extra names a [[wikilink]] can use to reach this memory, on top
 of its title. Each is normalised to a slug, so both "SEO Plan" and
 "seo-plan" match. Use this on import/migration to carry a note's original
 filename (e.g. the Obsidian vault slug) so `[[filename-slug]]` resolves to
 the memory even after its title was rewritten. Optional.

body.description: body is the memory content (markdown welcome).

private.description:
private, when true, stores the memory author-private: visible only to you,
 never returned by anyone else's recall. Use it when the memory summarises
 sensitive material. It only tightens - leaving it false does not override a
 restriction the server inherits from restricted content you read this session.

project.description: project scopes the memory (per-project memory); empty = space-wide.

space.description:
space optionally selects which of your spaces to act in (an id or name
 from list_spaces). Omit it when you belong to a single space.

supersedes.description:
supersedes optionally names the id of an EXISTING memory to replace,
 regardless of its title. Use it to be certain you are updating a specific
 memory rather than trusting a title match - and to heal a near-miss fork
 (e.g. "Deploy gotcha" vs "Deployment gotcha") by superseding the old memory
 with the corrected title in one call. The id must be a memory in this space
 that you can write, or the call errors. When set, the title-match path is
 bypassed; leave it empty for the default conversational behaviour.

tags.description: tags label the memory for later filtering (created in the space if new).

title.description:
title names the memory; defaults to the body's first line. Re-using a
 title within a project supersedes that memory.

type.description:
type is an OPTIONAL light classifier for the memory. Suggested values:
 decision, how-to, gotcha, reference, person, meeting. Free text - any label
 is accepted and it may be left empty (untyped). It informs recall filtering
 and display; it is not enforced.

name: remember

restricted.description:
restricted is true when the memory was stored private (author-private or a
 shared private project) - because you set private, or because it was derived
 from restricted content you read this session and the server scoped it down
 so it cannot leak. Surfaced so a scoping-down is visible, not silent.

title: Remember something
